title: Slavery in Rome
objective: After this level you can explain how slavery shaped Roman society and what freed slaves could become.
summary: Enslaved people, taken by war, piracy and birth, did every kind of work. Many were freed, and a citizen’s freed slave became a citizen.

cards.headline: In Rome, a doctor, a teacher and a miner could all be enslaved.
Property under the law
cards.body: Enslaved people made up a large share of the population of Roman Italy. People were enslaved through war, piracy and trade, and children born to enslaved mothers were enslaved too. Under Roman law an enslaved person was property, with no legal rights of their own.

cards.headline: Every kind of work
cards.body: Enslaved people worked in mines, on farms and in households. Some served as teachers, doctors and secretaries. Romans also often freed enslaved people, a practice called manumission.

cards.fact: A citizen’s freed slave usually became a Roman citizen.
cards.context: Their children had full rights. Some freedmen grew rich, and Claudius used freedmen as powerful officials.

cards.headline: Slavery: understood
learned: War, piracy and birth fed slavery
Freed slaves of citizens became citizens

options.label: Selling a slave at public auction

questions.explanation: Manumission was the freeing of an enslaved person, which Romans did often.

questions.prompt: What legal status did a person freed by a citizen usually gain?

options.label: A seat in the Senate
options.rationale: Their children gained full rights, not office.

questions.explanation: A person freed by a citizen usually became a citizen, and their children had full rights.
